negative_findings: No univariate model survives Benjamini-Yekutieli or Holm over the full 2010Q1-2026Q2 sample: 0 of about 396 tests in each target x h family and 0 of 4,752 globally. Best family BY q = 0.15.
No multivariate model (theory, penalised, PCA, combination, trees) survives BY within its 30-model family in any sample. Best q about 0.15.

Penalised regressions on all core features (LASSO, elastic net, ridge) mostly lose to the AR for d_margin, og and d_og. OOS R2 vs base -0.03 to -1.0; e.g. elastic net d_margin h=2 RMSE ratio 1.41, LASSO 1.21.

LASSO selection is unstable. LASSO keeps 5-18 of about 188 candidates per origin. The top full-period selection frequency is only 0.5-0.7, and sub-period frequencies swing from 0% to 100%: e.g. Norwegian food import prices are selected at 100% of d_margin_r4 origins in 2010-14 and 10% in 2015-19.

Theory-guided margin models built on price-cost gap + FX + electricity, FAO + USD + oil, pass-through (food CPI/PPI changes) or the Nordic price-cost gap do not beat the AR: RMSE ratio 1.00-1.18 at all horizons.

The d_og theory models specified ex ante in change form (food CPI dyoy, real wage dyoy, confidence d4) add nothing on the og-level base: ratios 1.01-1.08. Only the level versions on og work, and only at h=0.
Current-quarter food CPI (nw_food_cpi_xvat_yoy, w_food_cpi_xvat_yoy) does not improve organic-growth forecasts beyond og's own persistence: RMSE ratio 1.00-1.13.
Organic-growth gains from combinations and PCA are concentrated in 2021Q3-2023Q4. Excluding it, combination ratios are 0.99-1.00 (not significant).
Most rolling-4Q margin (d_margin_r4) gains vanish outside the inflation episode. Nothing beats the BIC-selected AR at h=0-1.
Changes in 10-year yields look like the best margin predictors over the full sample (-7 to -10% RMSE), but the RMSE ratio is about 1.00 excluding 2021Q3-23Q4.
PCA with 3 or more factors and PCA with BIC-chosen k are worse than PCA with 1 factor and often worse than the AR. Gradient boosting on residuals is worse than the base almost everywhere.
Real-time top-k selection with adaptive k is not better than plain equal weights. comb_top1 (follow the past winner) is 1-26% worse than the base.

Easter calendar terms hurt out of sample: AR+cal RMSE is 6-12% above pure AR for d_margin, og and d_og. The pre-committed AR+cal base was therefore replaced; against it, macro models looked spuriously good.
For d_margin at h=2 the zero-change forecast beats every AR. Macro models built on the AR barely recover to the zero benchmark; only PCA with 1 factor beats it, by 2.2%.
Directional accuracy is rarely improved: d_margin h=0 base 74% vs combinations 68-70%. The exception is the Nordic og nowcast (68% vs 56%).
Diebold-Mariano tests against the best benchmark are insignificant for every multivariate model except comb_all_mean for d_margin_r4 at h=2 (p=0.018).
key_numbers: Out-of-sample quarters: 66 (2010Q1-2026Q2), 56 excluding 2021Q3-23Q4, 50 excluding COVID and inflation, 46 from 2015, 36 from 2015 excluding inflation. Expanding window re-estimated every quarter; univariate burn-in from 2006Q1.
Tests per sample: 4,752 univariate (12 target x h cells x about 396) and 360 multivariate. oos_results.csv has 52,035 rows: target x h x base variant x model x sample.
d_margin AR OOS R2 vs zero: 0.28 / 0.02 / -0.09; hit rate 74% at h=0. og-level AR for d_og: OOS R2 vs zero 0.49 / 0.47 / 0.40.
Nordic og nowcast (food CPI ex VAT + real wage + confidence): RMSE -5.7% (CW p=0.004); excluding inflation -7.8% (p=0.010); 2015+ -7.2% (p=0.003).
d_margin input-cost theory model at h=0: RMSE -4.7% (CW p=0.031); excluding inflation -3.8% (p=0.006).
d_margin PCA with 1 factor: RMSE ratio 0.963 / 0.958 / 0.939 (CW p 0.036 / 0.014 / 0.039). Equal-weight combination: 0.985 / 0.984 / 0.984 (CW p 0.08 / 0.03 / 0.02).

Best single features ex post (full sample): d_margin 0.931 / 0.901 / 0.905; og 0.945 / 0.934 / 0.878; d_og 0.932 / 0.932 / 0.891; d_margin_r4 0.894 / 0.844 / 0.794. Bootstrap null mean of the best ratio is about 0.93-0.97, so these are only modestly better than chance.
Share of univariate models beating the base: og/d_og 34-42% vs 13-20% under the null (bootstrap p<=0.025); d_margin 28-35% vs about 15% (p 0.05-0.125).

Only multiple-testing survivors: w_unemp_d4 for og at h=2 excluding inflation (BY q<0.001 globally); in the 2015+ sample, no_earn_idx_food_manuf_q__yoy for d_og at h=2 (Holm) and se_eursek__yoy for d_og at h=0 (2015+ excluding inflation, Holm).

Live forecasts (as of 2026-10-06), 2026Q3 / 2026Q4 / 2027Q1. d_margin AR +0.37 / +0.17 / +0.12 pp; combination +0.36 / +0.14 / +0.07. d_og og-level AR -1.18 / -0.57 / -3.50 pp. og AR -0.40 / -0.11 / +0.03 %. d_margin_r4 AR +0.23 / +0.18 / +0.29 pp. Expected errors: about 1.0-1.3 pp for d_margin, 3.3-3.6 pp for organic growth.
caveats: findings.md was not written: the harness blocks subagents from writing report .md files. All findings are in this output; tables and figures are in the oos directory.

The base was changed after the benchmark race (disclosed). The pre-committed AR+Easter base was replaced by pure AR (d_margin, og, d_margin_r4) and by the og-level AR (d_og), because the calendar terms hurt OOS and the d_og-own-lag AR is far worse. The decision used benchmark performance only and makes the test harder. All models were also run on the pre-committed base; see the 'variant' column in oos_results.csv.

d_og and og forecasting are essentially the same problem, because og_py ~ og(t-4) is known in advance. Organic-growth conclusions should be read from the og results, or from d_og on the og-level base with level-form features.

Ex-post picks are optimistic by construction: the 'best single feature', the 'best theory model' and PCA with 1 factor (1 of 6 PCA variants) were chosen on full-sample RMSE. Only the combinations, LASSO/ridge/EN, PCA-BIC and the trees are fully real-time.
The 2021Q3-2023Q4 episode (10 quarters) dominates many full-sample gains; always read the ex-inflation columns. Gains of 2-5% RMSE over 56-66 quarters are within one or two large errors.

Macro data are latest vintage (revisions not handled), so national-accounts and real-wage results are mildly optimistic. Publication lags are respected via C.align realtime. Composite geographic weights use annual-report shares published after year end.

Pandemic quarters 2020Q1-2021Q2 are excluded from estimation but included in evaluation; the excovinfl2010 sample drops them too. d_og definition-break quarters are down-weighted in estimation (w_d_og) but evaluated unweighted.

The bootstrap null (AR(4) target with block-bootstrapped residuals, real features) has no 2022-23-type episode, so the 'more models beat the base than chance' result partly reflects that single episode.
Live forecasts skip models whose features are not yet published as of 2026-10-06 (e.g. September CPI): 174 of 196 univariate models are available, and the Nordic og nowcast model is unavailable.

No bug found in common.py. Usage note: C.align shifts within the panel's own index, which ends at 2026Q3, so F must be reindexed before aligning to forecast beyond the panel (live_forecasts.py does this).

Implementation notes. The arcal multivariate file (forecasts_multi_arcal.pkl) came from the first run. That run's linear stage had an exploding-coefficient bug from exact collinearity of the two Easter measures in short windows. It was fixed with a pseudo-inverse and all linear forecasts were regenerated; the multi stage uses its own least-squares solver and was unaffected. Penalised paths use coordinate-descent tolerance 1e-4 (minor convergence warnings at the smallest penalties). Clark-West and Diebold-Mariano use Newey-West with 4 lags, implemented in numpy and checked to match statsmodels exactly.
